page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for high-throughput parallel compute and machine learning tasks. It is provisioned on the KVM hypervisor using an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The instance is allocated 16 shared vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio, alongside 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by 3 NVIDIA L40S Ada Lovelace GPUs supplying a combined 144 GB of VRAM. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute and memory subsystem performance. In single-core testing, the AMD CPU delivers top-tier results with a stress-ng single-core score of 4184.96 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2922.0. Multi-core performance remains strong, scoring 66959.75 in stress-ng and 20598.0 in Geekbench. The memory architecture exhibits top-tier write throughput at 203.06 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks, accompanied by strong read speeds reaching 305.74 GB/sec uncached and 3766.69 GB/sec cached. Advanced instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512_VNNI, and AVX-512_BF16), boosting data compression and cryptographic operations, as reflected in single-threaded gzip throughput of 44.95 GB/sec.

The 3 NVIDIA L40S GPUs deliver top-tier performance for artificial intelligence workloads. In large language model benchmarks, the configuration achieves 13764.25 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 489.84 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M model, alongside 6015.0 tokens/sec prompt processing and 129.4 tokens/sec text generation on a 7B model. These metrics highlight high density for real-time inference across multiple medium-sized models simultaneously.

Workloads best suited for this instance include distributed AI model inference, computer vision pipelines, image processing, and rendering. The combination of 144 GB of GPU memory, high single-core CPU speeds, and 192 GB of host RAM offers substantial capacity for data ingestion, though workloads requiring extensive local disk I/O must account for the absence of integrated local storage.
description: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 16 vCPUs (16 physical cores), 192.0 GB of RAM, and 3 NVIDIA L40S GPUs delivering 144 GB of aggregate VRAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture and AVX-512 support, the system features top-tier single-core performance alongside robust uncached memory write bandwidth of 203.06 GB/sec. The triple-L40S configuration delivers top-tier LLM inference speeds, reaching 6015.0 prompt tokens/sec and 129.4 generation tokens/sec on 7B models. With no bundled local storage, persistent disks must be externally attached. This configuration is built for AI inference, batch computer vision workloads, and parallel processing.
